question: Two trains having lengths of 210 m and 140 m are running at speeds of 80 km/h and 150 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 150 − 80 = 70 km/h = 70 × (5/18) = 175/9 m/s.

Total distance to cross = Sum of lengths = 210 + 140 = 350 m.

Time taken to cross = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 350 ÷ (175/9) = (350 × 9) / 175 = 18 seconds.

Converting seconds to minutes = 18 ÷ 60 = 0.3 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.3 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the slower train (L₁) = 210 m

Length of the faster train (L₂) = 140 m

Speed of the slower train (S₁) = 80 km/h

Speed of the faster train (S₂) = 150 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₂ − S₁

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

Total Distance = Sum of the lengths of both trains = L₁ + L₂
